TimeIndex::is_unique¶

Back to TimeIndex API Reference

Signature¶

bool TimeIndex::is_unique() const

Whether Every Instant Appears Once¶

is_unique() returns true when no stored instant occurs more than once. It compares epoch-nanosecond identity, so two textual timestamps that denote the same instant are duplicates even if their offsets were written differently.

Uniqueness and ordering answer separate questions. A monotonic axis may contain ties and therefore be non-unique; an unordered axis may still contain only distinct instants. Use this query before operations whose meaning assumes one case per timestamp. Use unique() only when a new axis with duplicates removed is actually required.

To ask the inverse question without adding a duplicate public method, write !index.is_unique().

Trivial And Unordered Axes¶

Empty and one-element indices are unique because neither can contain a repeated pair. The result does not depend on timezone presentation or sort direction. For monotonic axes the implementation compares neighbors with constant memory. For an unordered axis it tracks observed nanosecond values in a hash set so duplicates separated by other timestamps are still detected.

Examples¶

Example 1. A normal ordered axis is unique.

auto index = pluss::timeindex::make({
    "2024-11-01T00:00:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:20:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:40:00Z",
});
std::cout << std::boolalpha << index.is_unique() << "\n";

Output¶

true

Example 2. Equal neighboring instants make a monotonic axis non-unique.

auto tied = pluss::timeindex::make({
    "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "2025-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
    "2025-01-01T01:00:00Z",
});
std::cout << std::boolalpha << tied.is_unique() << "\n";

Output¶

false

Example 3. Separated duplicates are detected on a deliberately unordered axis.

auto separated = pluss::timeindex::make({
    "2025-01-01T02:00:00Z",
    "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "2025-01-01T01:00:00Z",
    "2025-01-01T02:00:00Z",
}, false);
std::cout << std::boolalpha << separated.is_unique() << "\n";

Output¶

false

Example 4. Empty and singleton axes satisfy the predicate.

auto empty = pluss::timeindex::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{});
auto one = pluss::timeindex::make("2025-01-01T00:00:00Z");
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "empty=" << empty.is_unique() << "\n"
          << "one=" << one.is_unique() << "\n";

Output¶

empty=true
one=true

Cost And Allocation¶

The result is a native C++ bool. Monotonic input is checked in O(n) time with O(1) auxiliary memory. Unordered input remains O(n) expected time but may allocate O(n) hash storage. The TimeIndex itself is not modified.
